Chagres protects forest landscapes connected to the river of the same name. River excursions reveal the banks and tropical vegetation, while traveling by dugout canoe makes the water central to exploring the park. Here, nature exists alongside the lives of local communities.

Visits to Emberá settlements introduce travelers to the residents' culture and traditions. The encounter adds stories about the community's relationship with the river and its surroundings to the forest scenery. Chagres offers a chance to experience Panama's natural landscapes and living cultural traditions on a single trip from the capital.

A journey along the Chagres begins on the water, between forested banks. A traditional canoe takes travelers to Emberá communities to learn about local music, crafts and everyday life.

Near Gamboa, the river connects with the waterway system of the Panama Canal. The surrounding forest offers a different view of Panama: after city streets and canal locks, birds can be heard and green riverbanks stretch into view. The particular community and river route depend on the itinerary selected.

## The City and Its Ancient History

Chalchuapa lies in the department of Santa Ana in western El Salvador. For travelers, the city is best known for its archaeological sites, where evidence survives of the long development of pre-Columbian settlements and ceremonial centers.

The main stops on an archaeological visit are [Tazumal](/el-salvador/place/tazumal/) and [Casa Blanca](/el-salvador/place/casa-blanca-archaeological-site/). These are separate parks, so visiting one does not replace exploring the other.

## Tazumal and Casa Blanca

Tazumal is known for its large stepped structures. Casa Blanca reveals another part of ancient Chalchuapa, with excavated ceremonial buildings and traces of an early settlement. Both complexes are especially rewarding to explore with a guide who can explain how centers of daily life and ritual changed over time.

Museum displays add context to the buildings: individual artifacts and archaeological findings connect the stone platforms with the lives of people who inhabited the region.

## Chalchuapa on the Itinerary

On the [“Best of El Salvador” tour](/el-salvador/tour/el-salvador-san-salvador-suchitoto-gulf-of-fonseca/), Chalchuapa is visited on day three. The itinerary includes Tazumal and Casa Blanca before continuing to [Santa Ana](/el-salvador/place/santa-ana/) and [Ataco](/el-salvador/place/concepcion-de-ataco/). This combines archaeology with the architecture and crafts of western El Salvador.

Ada Tours' diving program names Champion as one of three possible dive sites near Floreana, alongside Cormorant Point and Enderby. Reef dives in this area may feature corals and sponges, sea lions, turtles, rays and several species of sharks. The specific dive site is chosen for the agreed outing; the itinerary does not promise visits to all three sites in one day.

Its adobe walls, courtyards and passageways reveal the heritage of the Chimú culture. The sandy coastal landscape brings out the textures of the walls and reliefs preserved from the ancient city.

Walking through the complex allows visitors to examine the layout of the structures and the decorative motifs on the walls. Exploring Chan Chan enriches a journey through northern Peru, where ancient monuments stand alongside modern cities and fishing communities. Nearby Huanchaco is another stop for discovering the culture of the Pacific coast.
